newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss gov't agrees quick action on Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss gov't agrees quick action on Holocaust fund.

text.p: The Swiss government agreed on Wednesday to create immediately a memorial fund that will tap contributions from banks and other businesses to aid victims of the Holocaust, Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti said.
Cotti said the cabinet was still working on how the government itself would address Jewish groups' demands that Switzerland pay compensation for what they call Swiss profiteering from World War Two.
"As an immediate first step, a special fund will be opened," Cotti said in a statement after a cabinet meeting, saying the account would draw on contributions from private business.

But he made clear that Berne would decide on its own contribution only after a international panel of historians now examining Switzerland's wartime role as a financial centre presented its first findings in the next few months.

Galvanised by international pressure, the country's three bigest banks agreed last week to put up 100 million Swiss francs ($70 million) as a humanitarian gesture to aid Holocaust victims and their families. Other businesses pledged to follow suit.

The government is coordinating the fund, which is aimed at assuring Jewish groups and other critics that the Swiss are taking seriously allegations Swiss banks stonewalled families of Holocaust victims seeking dormant wealth.
